'''''Herniaria hirsuta''''' is a species of flowering plant in the family [[Caryophyllaceae]] known by the common name '''hairy rupturewort'''.<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |accessdate=2014-10-17 }}</ref><ref>{{PLANTS|id=HEHI7|taxon=Herniaria hirsuta|accessdate=19 January 2016}}</ref> It is native to Eurasia and North Africa, and it is known on other continents, including North America, as an [[introduced species]]. This is an annual herb with stems up to {{convert|20|cm|in|abbr=on|sigfig=1}} long usually growing prostrate along the ground. The small, fuzzy, pale green leaves are up to about a centimeter long and coat the stems. The [[inflorescence]]s appear in the leaf axils. Each contains three to eight hairy green [[sepal]]s and no petals. The fruit is a tiny bumpy [[Utricle (fruit)|utricle]] containing one seed.

This plant is used in [[Morocco]] as an [[Herbalism|herbal remedy]] for [[kidney stones]].<ref name=bju>Atmani, F., et al. (2003). Prophylaxis of calcium oxalate stones by ''Herniaria hirsuta'' on experimentally induced nephrolithiasis in rats. ''[[British Journal of Urology|British Journal of Urology  International]]'' 92:1 137-40.</ref><ref>Atmani, F. (2004). Effect of aqueous extract from ''Herniaria hirsuta'' L. on experimentally nephrolithiasic rats. ''[[Journal of Ethnopharmacology]]'' 95:1 87-93.</ref><ref name=ju>Atmani, F. (2004). Extract from ''Herniaria hirsuta'' coats calcium oxalate monohydrate crystals and blocks their adhesion to renal epithelial cells. ''Journal of Urology'' 172:4 1510-14.</ref>
